passage: Vishal hated writing lists. Words on paper felt like homework. But tomorrow was art day, and he needed to pack a ruler, a pencil and a bottle of water. On a small card he drew a tiny yellow pencil, a long ruler with stripes and a blue bottle with a cap. He propped the card against the mirror. The next morning, his little sister Avni came in while he was getting dressed. "What's that?" "My list. Look, what do you see?" "Pencil, ruler, water!" Vishal grinned. He packed all three, and later drew her a card for her own bag.

qa.q: What did Vishal draw on the card?
qa.a: Vishal drew a pencil, a ruler and a bottle.

qa.q: How does Vishal feel about writing lists, and what does he do about it?
qa.a: Vishal dislikes writing because it feels like homework, so he draws pictures that he enjoys and can understand at a glance.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Vishal use if he loses the card, and why?
qa.a: Vishal could keep the items always in the same spot in the bag or check them against a list at the door. A fixed place needs no reading.

qa.q: How does Avni experience Vishal's picture list?
qa.a: Avni read the pictures at once and later got a card of her own, so Avni finds it easy to understand and probably enjoys having a list too.

grounding: A boy who dislikes writing draws a small pencil, ruler and bottle on a card, and the pictures help him and his younger sister remember what to pack.

subtype: Approach: drawing tiny pictures next to each item [Action]
passage: Saurabh hated writing lists. The letters came out slow and crooked, and he never read them later anyway. So on Sunday night, before the school week, he took a card and drew instead. A stubby pencil. A ruler with tiny lines. A water bottle with a cap. A lunch box with steam curling up. His father, Kishore, watched from the sofa. "Where are the words?" "Don't need them. I look, I pack." On Monday morning he glanced at the card taped to the cupboard and had everything in the bag in two minutes. By Wednesday his little sister Minu, who couldn't read yet, had taped a card of her own beside his, with a crayon, an apple and a sock.

qa.q: What did Saurabh draw on the card?
qa.a: A stubby pencil, a ruler with tiny lines, a water bottle with a cap and a lunch box with steam.

qa.q: How did Saurabh feel about writing lists before he tried pictures?
qa.a: He hated it and felt frustrated, because his letters came out slow and crooked.

qa.q: What could Saurabh add to make his picture card even more useful?
qa.a: He could draw a tick box beside each picture, so he can mark items off as he packs.

qa.q: How does the picture card look to Minu?
qa.a: For Minu, who can't read yet, pictures are something she can use herself, so she is excited to make her own card.

grounding: It shows a boy who dislikes writing drawing tiny pictures of what to pack, which works for him and his younger sister.

passage:
"Pradeep bhaiya, what's that?"
"My packing card, Swati. Look. Pencil box, ruler, bottle, tiffin, sports shoes."
"There are no words."
"Words are boring. I drew them. I see the shoe, I pack the shoe."
"Why is the tiffin smiling?"
"So I don't forget it. Last week I forgot it."
"Can you make me one?"
"You make it. What do you need for nursery?"
"Crayons. Napkin. My water bottle. Teddy."
"Teddy's not allowed."
"Teddy's allowed on Friday."
"Fine. Draw a teddy with an F on it."
Next morning Swati packed her bag first and waved the card at him.

qa.q: Why did Pradeep draw the tiffin smiling?
qa.a: He drew it smiling so he wouldn't forget it, since he forgot it last week.

qa.q: How did Swati feel when she waved her card at Pradeep the next morning?
qa.a: She felt proud and pleased, because she had packed her bag first using her own picture card.

qa.q: What else could Pradeep do to help Swati use her card?
qa.a: He could check her bag with her against the card for the first few days, until the habit is hers.

qa.q: How does the picture card look to Swati?
qa.a: Swati, who likes the smiling tiffin, sees it as fun and easy, and wants one of her own.

grounding: It shows a boy drawing little pictures of what to pack, which also works for his younger sister.
